newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Nov 13.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Nov 13.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

After the resignation of Australian Rugby League chief executive John Quayle yesterday, there seems to be few contenders from within the game to take up the vacant position. Club chief executives that may be regarded for the position do not want the job,nor do Geoff Carr, Greg Mitchell or Colin Love, who already work within the ARL administration. This may leave the ARL with no option but to recruit a new boss from outside the game. Page 30.

The A$100,000 Qantas Skins swimming meet will be held at the Sydney International Aquatic Centre on Saturday night and will see several young Australian swimmers who hope to break into the national side before the 2000 Olympic Games compete against more tan 20 Olympic medallists from 10 countries. Page 29.

Australian women's cricket captain Belinda Clark yesterday described New Zealand cricket as boring at the launch of the Women's National Cricket League at North Sydney Oval. Clark said the six-week national one-day league will do little to prepare the Autralian team for the tour to New Zealand in February, as the Kiwis play an "interesting game of cricket which we don't agree with". Page 26.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Soccer Australia chairman David Hill will arrive in London today to meet with a number of British-based candidates for the position of Australian coach. One of the main candidates is former England manager Terry Venables, along with two other leading Briish managers Jack Charlton and Howard Wilkinson. Page 48.

Melbourne Cup winner Saintly arrived safe and well in Japan yesterday for Sunday week's A$5 million Japan Cup, after a long flight from Melbourne. Yet trainer Bart Cummings' plans are behind schedule as Saintly's jockey Darren Beadman faces the Victorian Racing Club's Racing Appeals Board today after being charged with careless riding and suspended until November 30 after riding Dashing Eagle in the VRC Oaks last Thursday. Page 47.

British golfer Laura Davies arrived in Australia from Japan yesterday morning, prepared to compete in the A$350,000 Australian Ladies' Masters this week. While Alice Springs bookmakers have Davies to win the tournament at 5-2, Davies herself feels threatned by Australian golfer Karrie Webb, whom she says she thinks has got "something up her sleeve". Page 47. --
THE AGE

Former Australian cricket captain Allan Border has tipped Victorian opener Matthew Elliott to take up David Boon's vacant No. 3 position in the Test team to play against the West Indies in Brisbane late next week, and says he believes New South Wales leftander Michael Bevan should be retained in the middle order. Page C20.

After being staunchly opposed to playing matches at Optus Oval, AFL club Collingwood has agreed to play a one-off practice match against Carlton at the venue in February. The new-look ground will boast a 35,000-seat Legends Stand, and the match will be ued by both clubs to boost membership and prepare them for the pre-season Ansett Cup. Page C18.

The Australian Championship Circuit surfing title race was decreased from five to three surfers yesterday in day one of the Island Classic at Phillip Island. Manly surfer Ryan Alagich was eliminated from both the contest and the championship for failing to appear at his heat, while Sunshine Coast teenager Nick Wallace caused an upset as he put an end to Richard Marsh's hopes. Page C18.
HERALD SUN

Adelaide Giants pitcher Troy Scoble received the stiffest suspension ever from the Australian Baseball League when he received an eight-game suspension and a A$200 fine for his role in an ugly bench-clearing brawl against the Melbourne Monarchs last Frida night. Page 77.

Drew Ginn, the newest member of the Australian rowing team the Oarsome Foursome, showed less prowess in the water yesterday as a wildcard entrant in the Australian championship surfing circuit Island Classic at Cat Bay, Phillip Bay. The former cadet champion and recreational surfer crashed out of his heat. Page 78.

David Boon's testimonial match at the Melbourne Cricket Ground was frowned upon by the Australian Cricket Board yesterday, and had the ACB stuck to its policy, it would not have gone ahead. Testimonial matches are becoming popular for ageing stars to cash in on their popularity and status, and the concerns of officials could become a sore point between them and players. Page 76.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Rugby union winger Ben Tune realises the Wallabies match against Ulster on Saturday at Belfast is the last chance he has to make it to the Test side to play against Ireland at Landsdowne Road. Tune has played six rugby union Tests for Australia this season, but his form has seen him drop his Test spot hopes behind those of Tim Horan, Joe Roff and David Campese. Page 76.

The West Indies cricket team collapsed early before calmly returning to form (8-218) in an invitational match against a Northern Territory Invitation XI (170) yesterday. The team included seven Sheffield Shield players and four promising locals, includin spinner Mark Hatton, who claimed 3-24, including Brian Lara for 27. Page 75.

New South Wales cricket captain Greg Matthews will meet with coach Geoff Lawson to discuss the Blues' match against Victoria. The game saw Victoria needing 457 to win, yet a strong partnership between Matthew Elliott and Darren Berry saw the Blues win byonly 58 runs. Page 74.
